bibliographic_scope.title: A new approach to the synthesis of conjugated polymer–nanocrystal composites for heterojunction optoelectronics
bibliographic_scope.authors: Andrew Watt; Elizabeth Thomsen; Paul Meredith; Halina Rubinsztein-Dunlop

preparation_details.stock_vs_dose: Sulfur0.08g in10mL toluene is full-stock formulation; injected stock aliquot is1mL. No full-stock charge is substituted.
preparation_details.reagents: SigmaAldrich, used without further purification; lead-acetate hydrate and polymer molecular weight/dispersity unspecified.
preparation_details.apparatus: 25mL three-neck flask with Liebig condenser, as reported; liquid-volume context retained separately.
preparation_details.sampling_quench: Samples may be withdrawn at any stage and quenched in toluene at ambient temperature. This optional sampling method is not made a mandatory step of the bulk workup; no Celsius value or quench volume is inferred.
preparation_details.redispersion_scope: Examples of desired solvents, not a specified mixed-solvent charge.

structural_scope.TEM_time: Not separately specified for Figure1;4±2nm is not inherited by each timed optical sample.

size_nm.estimator: Average; statistic and weighting not defined

structural_scope.coordinates: No atomic-coordinate asset or numerical cell parameter supplied.

polymer_free_control.scope: Qualitative source control; separate charges/schedule, size/phase data and an exact independent protocol are not supplied. No additional structural pair inferred.

source_interpretation.topic: Polymer as growth medium and matrix
source_interpretation.text: The authors grow PbS directly within MEH-PPV, using the polymer as a growth-controlling medium and continuous conductive matrix. They propose steric effects of the polymer chain, rather than charged surfactant groups, as the main growth-control mechanism. Polymer conformation and passivation are not measured atom by atom.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Synthesis concept and growth discussion

source_interpretation.text: The cleaned material forms a continuous thin composite film containing nonaggregated, polydisperse PbS nanocrystals. The reported average size is4±2nm; the TEM aliquot harvest time is not separately stated. Cubic PbS is identified by selected-area diffraction along[111]. The2µm diffraction area is not a nanocrystal size.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, TEM discussion and Figure1

source_interpretation.text: Polymer emission decreases from the pre-injection reference through3- and15-minute samples. The authors interpret this as electronic coupling. They argue that the similar spectral shape accounts for reabsorption and that the lack of a free-ion absorption signature disfavors complex formation, while acknowledging dielectric changes could produce similar effects. No charge-transfer rate or absolute quantum yield is supplied.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, Figure2 and electronic-coupling discussion

source_interpretation.topic: Boundaries of the lifetime and control evidence
source_interpretation.text: The main cites ESI lifetime measurements as further support, but that ESI is not reviewed here. The authors also report bulk PbS without polymer; a separately specified recipe and quantitative control characterization are absent. Neither statement creates an invented additional synthesis–structure row.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 1–2, ESI footnote and polymer-free control discussion
